arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: Custom chatbot powered by OpenAI's GPT-4o API during the Frisbee AUT; asks probing questions and offers new perspectives without direct task solutions. Copy-paste disabled; participants instructed to use it as a collaborative thinking tool (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

arms.name: Human-Search
arms.description: Custom text-only web search engine during the Frisbee AUT; no visual stimuli, used for inspiration, with the same copy-paste restriction (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

estimates.question: with_ai

estimates.notes: Unadjusted post-test arm means and SDs are from Table 2; no mean difference, mean SE, confidence interval, or unadjusted test statistic was calculated. The paper_effect is the printed zero-order correlation between binary condition and post-test creativity in Table 1, describing the same full-sample unadjusted comparison. Section 3.4 codes Human-Search as 0 and Human-AI as 1. Table 1 marks the correlation with three asterisks but prints no significance legend for that table; p_value is therefore null. The participant unit follows the arm participant counts, participant-level ANCOVA, and the description of individual participant trajectories in Section 4, although the response-aggregation rule is unstated. Tables 1 and 2 are embedded images absent from extracted PDF text and markdown; their exact printed cells were checked visually in memory after extracting the page text and running find_tables(). Row quotes reproduce the row label and selected cells, in their printed order. This record and the ANCOVA record analyze the same people and output; they are not independent estimates. The contradictory adjusted columns in Table 2 do not alter the unadjusted columns transcribed here.

estimates.notes: ANCOVA controls for baseline creativity, age, work experience, gender, and race (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Sections 3.4 and 4). These are baseline variables; this record is distinct from the excluded mediation model controlling for post-test ideation. IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED SOURCE CONFLICT: treatment_mean and control_mean faithfully transcribe the arm labels in the Section 4 results prose. Table 2 assigns the same adjusted means and confidence limits to the opposite arms, as reproduced in the final source quote. This extraction does not establish which adjusted labels are correct. The positive difference is printed in the prose, not calculated or obtained by reversing a table sign. The CI fields are the Human-AI adjusted mean interval as labeled in prose, not an interval for the difference; the Human-Search adjusted mean interval is retained in its source quote because the schema has no separate control-mean CI fields. The reported partial eta squared is also retained in the ANCOVA test source quote; the single paper_effect object records the reported Cohen's d. Its standardizer is not specified. No ANCOVA coefficient SE, difference SE, difference CI, or adjusted SD is supplied, and none is derived. The unadjusted SDs are kept only in the separate unadjusted record. Both records concern the same sample and output.

not_extracted.what: Self-reported ideation at pre-test and post-test, including condition-to-ideation path coefficients
not_extracted.reason: Runco Ideational Behavior Scale self-reports, not scores of produced output (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 3.3; PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Table 3).
Self-reported confidence collected before treatment; not an output-scored creativity outcome (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99], Sections 3.2-3.3).

not_extracted.what: Baseline fork AUT creativity and within-condition pre-test/post-test changes
not_extracted.reason: Baseline output preceded random assignment, and a within-arm time change is not a randomized AI-versus-comparator contrast. Task order was fixed, so these are neither randomized first-round/paired AI comparisons nor after-AI outcomes (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2; PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 3.4; PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Table 2 and Figure 1).

not_extracted.what: Indirect condition effect on creativity through ideation and ideation-to-creativity path
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses, excluded by extraction rule 5; the mediator is self-reported ideation (PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Section 4 and Table 3).

not_extracted.what: Direct condition effect on creativity in the path model controlling for post-test ideation
not_extracted.reason: Adjusted for a variable measured after treatment; this mediator-adjusted direct effect is ineligible, unlike the extracted baseline-adjusted ANCOVA (PDF p. 6 [printed p. 100], Section 4 and Table 3).

not_extracted.what: CSE moderation, conditional indirect effects, index of moderated mediation, and high-minus-low conditional indirect-effect comparison
not_extracted.reason: Moderation and moderated-mediation results, including condition-by-CSE interactions for creativity and ideation and effects at selected CSE levels; not full-sample total treatment contrasts (PDF pp. 6-7 [printed pp. 100-101], Section 4, Table 3, and Figure 2).

not_extracted.what: Open-ended self-report of how participants used the assigned tool
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported condition confirmation, not creativity or diversity scored on produced output; no eligible treatment-effect statistic is reported for it (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).

open_items: Adjusted arm labels remain unresolved: the Section 4 prose and Table 2 assign the adjusted means and confidence limits to opposite arms. The ANCOVA record is explicitly a transcription of the prose, not a resolution of this conflict (PDF pp. 5-6 [printed pp. 99-100]).

The paper does not print the total or arm-specific randomized counts before exclusions or exclusions by arm. Recruitment and final analysis counts are distinct; randomized counts remain null (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.1).
The exact scoring model/version, score range, and rule for aggregating alternative-use responses into participant creativity scores are not stated (PDF pp. 4-5 [printed pp. 98-99], Section 3.3).
The standardizer of the reported Cohen's d is not stated; do not assume it is a control-arm or pooled participant-level SD (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Sections 3.4 and 4).

The adjusted contrast has no printed difference SE or difference CI. The printed CIs and SEs concern adjusted arm means and must not be treated as difference uncertainty (PDF p. 5 [printed p. 99], Section 4).
The intervention is identified as GPT-4o, but the exact dated model snapshot and release year are not stated; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 4 [printed p. 98], Section 3.2).
notes: Extraction A, 2026-10-11. Read the full markdown conversion from beginning to end, including all references; extracted text from all nine PDF pages with PyMuPDF. There is no appendix or stated supplement. Ran find_tables() on the methods/results pages; Table 3 was recoverable, while Tables 1 and 2 required visual inspection of their embedded images in memory. No files other than this extraction JSON were created or changed. No statistics were calculated or digitized from figures. All numeric stats and participant counts are transcribed, with printed precision retained in source quotes. The repeated pre/post assessments do not constitute randomized-order within-person AI exposure: assignment is between participants for the post-test, and within_person is null. There is one eligible output-scored composite and no across-people diversity or post-withdrawal output outcome. Preregistration and an explicit primary-outcome designation are not stated. Participant overlap with another paper is not reported; shared_sample null means unknown, not proven absence. The two estimates are alternative analyses of the same sample and outcome. The adjusted-label conflict is carried forward for reconciliation rather than silently corrected.
